<entry id="V00810">
<head-word>תָּפַח</head-word>
<hw-number>III</hw-number>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> = טָפַח II,
<italic>to drip, be moist.</italic></definition>
<notes> Tosef. Shebi. II, 14, v. תָּפַח I. B. Mets. 59
<sup>b</sup> Ms. R. 2, v. טָפַח II.—
<italic>Part. pass</italic>. תָּפוּחַ 
<italic>a</italic>) 
<italic>decaying</italic>. Sabb. 128
<sup>b</sup> top בשר ת' spoiled meat (Ms. M. תפל, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note).—
<italic>b</italic>) 
<italic>languishing, faint</italic> (from starvation). Snh. 63
<sup>b</sup> מצא תינוק שהיה ת' ומוטל באשפה he found a child that was faint and lying prostrated on a dunghill; Sifra B’ḥuck. Par. 2, ch. VI מצא אחד ת' ומוטל ברעב (insert תינוק); ib. שהיה מחזר על כל טְפוּחֵי רעב; Snh. l. c. תְּפוּחֵי he (Elijah) went around visiting all those languishing from starvation; Yalk. Lev. 675; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>a</sup> עד אלישׁע … דחליש וא' וכ' Ms. M. (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) until Elisha’s days nobody was ever sick and recovered; then Elisha came and prayed, and he recovered; (Ms. F. לא הוה איקצורי ואִיתַּפּוּחֵי there was no such a thing as being sick and recovering; בעי … למיחלש ואיתפוחי Elisha prayed for sickness and recovery); Yalk. <sense>
<number>—2)</number>

<sup>3</sup> Engl.</definition>
<notes> ed., s. v. Focus). Targ. Ps. CII, 4 (h. text מוקד).—Y. Sabb. III, beg., 5

<plural-form>Pl. תַּפְיָין</plural-form>. Targ. Y. Lev. XI, 35 (Bxt. טַפְיָין; h. text כירים). Targ. Y. Num. XXVI, 61 (not חפיין).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00821">
<head-word>תְּפִיסָה</head-word>
<head-word>תְּפִישָׂה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (תָּפַס) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>seizing, taking hold, possession; grasp, manipulation</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. 84
<sup>b</sup> top ור"ע ת' … כלל and according to R. Akiba does possession have no legal effect at all? Ḥull. 44
<sup>a</sup> עד כדי תְפִיסַת יד as much space as is covered by a grasp of the hand. Ned. V, 3 (46
<sup>a</sup>) אם יש לו בהן תפיסת יד (Y. ed. פוסתת̇) if he has an interest in them (the bath, or the wine or oil press which he has rented out); ib. 46
<sup>b</sup> וכמה ת' יד וכ' and how large must that interest be?… One-half, or one-third, or one-fourth. Ab. Zar. III, 5 מפני מה … שיש בה תפיסת ידי אדם (Y. ed. תְּפִישַׂת) why is it forbidden to make use of the wood of an Asherah (it being a natural object)? Because the hands of men had something to do with it (they planted it). Ib. 50
<sup>a</sup> שתים בת' לו two stones (of a 
<italic>merculis</italic>) within a grasp’s distance (four cubits). Tosef. Ḥull. VIII, 5 לא … שכולן ת' אחת (not שכולי) they forbid (two guests in an inn at the same table to eat, the one meat, and the other cheese) only when all of it is handled together; Ḥull. 107
<sup>b</sup> ת' אחת סלקא דעתך you cannot mean really handled together (wrapped together); אלא כעין ת' אחת but it means, with the appearance of belonging together. Tosef. Ter. III, 7 כל בית הגיתות תפו' אחת ed. Zuck. (Var. תפי') the whole wine-press room may be considered one concern; כיצד גת אחת … בזמן שכולן ת' אחת וכ' in what way? If there is one vat for two pits, or …, as long as they are all worked at the same time, you may take T’rumah or tithes from one for the other; אין כולם ת' אחת וכ' if they are not all worked at the same time, you cannot &c. Ib. כל בית הבד ת' אחת the whole oil press room may be considered one concern; a. fr.—Deut. R. s. 2 תפיסת קורצין, v. קְווּצּוֹת.—
<plural-form>Pl. תְּפִיסוֹת, תְּפִישׂ', תְּפוּ'</plural-form>. Ab. Zar. 8
<sup>b</sup> שתי ת' תפסה רומי וכ' twice Rome seized the empire (in the east), once in the days of queen Cleopatra, and once in the days of the Greeks. Ib. 50
<sup>a</sup> בשתי ת' at a distance of two grasps (eight cubits), v. supra. Y. Ter. II, 41
<sup>b</sup> bot. שהיה בלבו תפושה אחת … שתי תפוש' when he had intended to treat the wine in the press room as one concern, but reconsidered it in favor of two concerns; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>being taken, detention</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 13
<sup>18</sup> שהיו מפשפשים … תפיסת מצרים they examined their own deeds to find out why the detention in Egypt had happened to them; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition />
<notes> v. 
<xref rid="V00806">תְּפוּסָה</xref></notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00830">
<head-word>תִּפְלָה</head-word>
<head-word>תִּי'</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> תָּפַל)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> [
<italic>mud, slime</italic>,] 
<italic>frivolity, trivial cause; impropriety, indecency</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ab. Zar. 63
<sup>b</sup> (in Chald. dict.) כל למעוטי תי' שפיר דמי anything to diminish folly (idolatry) is right. Ib. 64
<sup>a</sup> ואלו למעט את הת' שפיר דמי Ms. M. (ed. ואלו למעוטי ת' שרי) but in this case, as it serves to diminish folly (the sin of כִּלְאַיִם), it is right. Tosef. Sot. VI, 8 אי אפשר לעמוד על תִּיפְלָתָם Var. (ed. Zuck. התָּפֵל) it is impossible to understand their frivolous ways; a. e.—Lam. R. to II, 14 נאמר בנביאי שומרון ת' … ירושלים ת' of the prophets of Samaria the word 
<italic>tiflah</italic> is used (Jer. XXIII, 13) …, and of the prophets of Jerusalem the word 
<italic>tiflah (tafel)</italic> is used (Lam. l. c.).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00831">
<head-word>תְּפִלָּה</head-word>
<head-word>תְּפִי'</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<pos> f.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> פָּלַל)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> [
<italic>intercession, pleading</italic>,] 
<italic>prayer</italic>, esp. 
<italic>T’fillah</italic>, the Prayer of Benedictions to be 
<pgbrk id="pg1687" />said three times every day, four times on the Sabbath and the festivals (v. 
<xref rid="M00548">מוּסַף</xref>), and five times on the Day of Atonement and public fast-days (v. נְעִילָה).</definition>
<notes> Taan. 2
<sup>a</sup> ומנלן דבת' and whence do you prove that the mention of, and the prayer for rain must be inserted in the T’fillah? Ib. עבודה שבלב זו ת', v. עֲבוֹדָה. Ber. IV, 1 תְּפִלַּת השחר the morning T’fillah, ת' המנחה the afternoon T’fillah &c. (v. respective determinants). Ib. 5
<sup>a</sup> אלו הם יסורין … בטול ת' sufferings of love are those with which no cessation of prayer is connected. Ib. 6
<sup>b</sup> הקובע מקום לתְפִלָּתוֹ he that has a regular place for his prayers. Ib. 31
<sup>b</sup> שאסור לישב … של ת' that it is forbidden to sit down within four cubits distance from one in prayer; a. v. fr.—Ib.
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. שומע ת' (abbrev. ש"ת) ‘hearer of prayer’, the fifteenth section of the Prayer of Benedictions which closes with, ‘blessed be thou, O Lord, the hearer of prayer.’—
<plural-form>Pl. תְּפִלּוֹת, תְּפִי'</plural-form>. Ib. 26
<sup>b</sup> ת' אבות תקנום the patriarchs introduced regular prayers. Ib. ת' כנגד תמידין תקנום prayers (T’filloth) have been instituted so as to correspond to the daily offerings. Sabb. 30
<sup>a</sup> כמה ת' ותחנונים ever so many prayers and supplications; a. v. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00834">
<head-word>תִּפְלוּת</head-word>
<head-word>תִּי'</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (תָּפַל; v. 
<xref rid="V00830">תִּפְלָה</xref>) 
<italic>frivolity, trivialness; obscenity</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Taan. IV, 68
<sup>d</sup> top, v. בְּכִיָּה. Y. Snh. II, 20
<sup>a</sup> top; Y. M. Kat. III, 83
<sup>d</sup> top קרע של ת' a wanton rent in a garment (without any religious significance); Bab. ib. 22
<sup>b</sup>. Num. R. s. 4
<sup>20</sup> כל העם … ובנו עונה דברים של ת' all the people said Halleluiah after the reader, and his son spoke some frivolous words. Ib. s. 10
<sup>3</sup> עובדי … בדברי ת' when the gentiles eat and drink, they engage in indecent talk. Ruth R. to I, 14; Ex. R. s. 5, a. e. כל נשיקות של ת' הן וכ' all kissing is of a frivolous nature, except the kiss of homage &c., v. נְשִׁיקָה. Sot. <entry id="V00843">
<head-word>תָּפַס</head-word>
<head-word>תָּפַשׂ</head-word>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> cmp. תָּפַף)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to seize, take hold on; to take effect</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. 84
<sup>b</sup> את תּוֹפֵס לבעל חוב וכ' thou seizest property in behalf of a creditor when the debtor owes others, ואמר ר' י' התופס וכ' and R. J. has decided that he who seizes in behalf of a creditor when there are other claimants has not taken legal possession. Ib. top והוא שת' מחיים (his possession is effectual) when he has seized it during the decedent’s life-time. Ab. Zar. 8
<sup>b</sup> (expl. קרטיסיס) יום שתָּפְסָה בו רומי מלכות the day when Rome took hold of the government (of the east, v. תְּפִיסָה). Y. Taan. IV, 68
<sup>c</sup> top היה משה תוֹפְשָׂן Moses held fast on them (the tablets). R. Hash. 4
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. תָּפַסְתָּ מרובה וכ', v. מוּעָט. B. Mets. 102
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. תְּפוֹס לשון אחרון hold to the latter expression, i.e. if an agreement contains two discrepant 
<pgbrk id="pg1688" />clauses, the second is legally recognized; Tem. 26
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. תפוס לשון ראשון the first clause (of a vow) is legally recognized. Yeb. 10
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. אין קידושין תּוֹפְסִין וכ', v. קִידּוּשׁ. Y. Dem. VI, 25
<sup>b</sup> תָּפְשָׂה מדת הדין וכ' justice takes hold on him &c., i.e. the full rigor of the law is applied against him &c. Num. R. s. 11
<sup>1</sup> (ref. to Prov. III, 34) אלו הנזירים שתּוֹפְשִׂים ענוה בעצמן וכ' that means the Nazarites who choose humility for themselves, who abstain from wine &c. Ib. 10
<sup>8</sup> ותְפָשָׂם and arrested them, v. לוּפָר. Snh. 64
<sup>a</sup> מפני מה תפסה תורה לשון מולך why does the Biblical text choose the word 
<italic>Molekh</italic> (in place of idol in general)? Y. Ber. VII, 11
<sup>c</sup> top, a. e. תופסין אותו seize him, take him to task, v. נַקְדָּן. Ab. Zar. 64
<sup>a</sup> דמי … מי תוֹפֶסֶת דמיה וכ' how about money which was realized by the sale of an idol, in the hands of a gentile? does the idol hold its equivalent in gentile hands or not?, i.e. does the money in gentile hands retain its character as compensation for an idol, and is it thus forbidden to a Jew? Ex. R. s. 15
<sup>20</sup> היה שלמה תופס פיו וכ' Solomon controlled his mouth, in order not to speak before &c. Gen. R. s. 12 כל … תופסין את הלשון וזה אינו תופס וכ' all other letters catch the tongue (require an effort of the organs of speech), but this (the Hé) does not catch &c. (is merely a breathing sound).—
<italic>Part. pass.</italic> תָּפוּס, תָּפוּשׂ; f. תְּפוּסָה, תְּפוּשָׂה &c. 
<italic>a</italic>) (cmp. אָחוּז s. v. אָחַז) 
<italic>holding</italic>. Y. Taan. l. c. היה משה ת' בטפחיים Moses was holding two handbreadths (of the tablets). Ex. R. s. 46, beg. היה ת' בלוחות וכ' he held the tablets, and would not believe that Israel had sinned. Sifra B’ḥuck. Par. 2, ch. VIII תְּפוּסֵי מעשה וכ' holding to the deeds of their fathers, generation after generation; a. e.—
<italic>b</italic>) 
<italic>seized, captured</italic>. Mekh. Mishp., s. 17 תפוסה the outraged woman, opp. מפותה the seduced.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִתְפַּס, נִתְפַּשׂ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be seized, arrested; to have one’s property seized; to be made responsible</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ex. R. s. 15
<sup>18</sup> בן בית שנ' על ידי בעל וכ' a domestic servant who was seized for his employer’s debt. Tosef. Ḥull. II, 24 נ' ע"ד מינות, v. מִינוּת. Ib. ונִתְפַּסְתִּי על וכ' and therefore I was arrested on the suspicion of heresy. Ab. Zar. 17
<sup>b</sup> כשנִתְפְּסוּ ר' אלעזר וכ' when R. El. a. R. H. b. T. were arrested (by Roman officials, for rebellious conduct). Ib. אשריך שנִתְפַּסְתָּ על וכ' happy art thou, for thou hast been arrested on one charge only, and woe me that I have been arrested on five charges. B. Bath. 16
<sup>b</sup> אין אדם נ' על צערו Ms. M. (ed. בשעת) no man is taken to account for what he speaks in his distress. Sabb. 33
<sup>b</sup> נִתְפָּסִים על הדור are seized for the debt (die for the sins) of their generation. Y. Keth. XIII, 35
<sup>d</sup> כל הנ' על חבירו חייב ליתן לו in every case if one’s property was seized for a neighbor’s debt, the latter has to reimburse him; ib. אין לך נ' וכ' in no case must he reimburse him, except in the case of 
<italic>annona</italic> and head-tax; Y. B. Kam. X, end, 7
<sup>c</sup>; Y. Ned. IV, beg. 38
<sup>c</sup>. Deut. R. s. 2, beg. (prov.) הוי זהיר שלא תִתָּפֵס מקום דבורך take care that thou be not caught on the spot where thou speakest (held to thy word); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְפִּיס</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to cause to be seized, cause to take hold</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Succ. IV, 54
<sup>d</sup> top ראה שהִתְפִּיסָתְךָ התורה לשון וכ' behold, the Law has made thee use the expression of endearment &c. Tem. 2
<sup>a</sup> הכל מַתְפִּיסִין בתמורה all persons can cause the seizure of the substitute together with the original by exchanging a consecrated animal (v. תְּמוּרָה). Ib. 9
<sup>a</sup> מי מַתְפִּיס בדבר שאינו שלו can one cause the seizure of a thing which is not his?; a. e.—[Ned. 11
<sup>b</sup>, sq. מתפיס, v. next w.]</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>תִּפֵּס, תִּפֵּשׂ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (v. 
<xref rid="I00667">טָפַס</xref>) 
<italic>to climb, rise</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 66, end (ref. to Prov. XXX, 28) באיזה זכות השממית מְתַפֶּשֶׂת בזכות וכ' for what merit does the spider (Esau-Rome) climb (rise to power)? For the merit of those hands (with which Esau nursed his father, by ref. to Gen. XXVII, 3</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition />
<notes>; Yalk. ib. 115; Yalk. Prov. 963 תְּתַפֵּשׂ.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pirel.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>תִּרְפֵּס, </binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, 
<italic>Hithparel</italic> הִתַּרְפֵּס same.</definition>
<notes> Y. Erub. V, 22
<sup>d</sup> top רואה אותו כי מִיתַּרְפֵּס ועולה מְתַרְפֵּס ויורד, (v. טָפַס) you look upon it (measure the distance for Sabbath purposes) as if one would climb up and climb down (the wady).</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<sense>
<definition>;

<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be seized, arrested</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Koh. XI, 4 (ed. Vien. מִתְפַּס).—Tem. 26
<sup>b</sup> למימרא דתחת לישנא דאִיתַּפּוּסֵי הוא shall we say that 
<italic>taḥath</italic> has the meaning of being arrested, i.e. if you say, this animal shall be 
<italic>taḥath</italic> (in the place of) that animal, it becomes consecrated according to the law of exchange (תְּמוּרָה)? Ib. תחת … לישנא דאתפוסי ולישנא דאחולי 
<italic>taḥath</italic> appears in the sense of being arrested and in the sense of redeeming; לישנא דאיתפוסי דכתיב וכ' in the sense of being arrested, as we read (Lev. XIII, 23) &c. Ib. 27
<sup>a</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be deposited</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. 107
<sup>b</sup> לא מִתְּפִיס, v. צְרָרָא I.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to hold one’s self, cling to</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ned. 11
<sup>b</sup> בהיתירא קא מתפיס he clings to the idea of permission, i.e. by saying, ‘this thing be unto me like flesh of a peace-offering after the blood has been sprinkled’, he proves that he means to emphasize the permission to enjoy the thing; אלא כגון … בעיקרו קא מתפיס ות' but in a case like this, when he puts down flesh of a peace-offering, and places some permitted food beside it, and says, ‘this be like this’: does he mean to refer to the original condition of the peace-offering &c.? (v. צִנְנָא). Ib. 12

<sup>b</sup>, v. צִנְנָא. Ib. 21
<sup>a</sup> חד בחבריה מתפיס (in saying, ‘and I’) each refers to him that spoke immediately before him; בקמא מִיתַּפְּסֵי they all refer to the first person; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

CIII, 20, sq.) עליונים ע"י שהן יכולין לעמוד בתַפְקִידָיו של וכ' because the celestial beings can stand by (always fulfill) the orders of the Lord, the text says, bless the Lord, ye all his hosts: but as to the earthly beings, who cannot (always) stand by the orders of the Lord, the text says, ‘bless the Lord, ye his messengers’; Yalk. <sense>
<number>—2)</number>

III, 1 המניח … ונ' בה ושברה if one left his pitcher on public ground, and another man came and struck against it, and broke it. <sup>b</sup>, a. e. (in Chald. dict.) אתי בהו לידי ת' one may be led to commit an offence through them; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<number>—2)</number>

<sup>b</sup> איזיל אֲתַקֵּין מילתא I will go and remedy something (do something to benefit the community). Ib. איכא מילתא דבעי לתַקּוּנֵי is there anything that requires to be remedied? Zeb. 15
<sup>a</sup> אפשר לתַקּוּנָהּ it can be remedied. Ib. 76

<sup>b</sup>. Keth. 85
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. לתקוני שדרתיך, v. עֲוַת; a. fr.—Esp. 
<italic>to make fit for use by separating the priestly gifts</italic>. Gen. R. s. 60 תַּקְּנַת אילין וכ' hast thou tithed those figs? Ib. תַּקַּנְתּוּהוּ have you tithed it (the barley)?; a. fr.—Part. pass. as ab. Ib. אפשר … דלא מְתַקְּנַן is it possible that R. Z. should have eaten of them when they were not tithed?; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to introduce, ordain, innovate, reform</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 33
<sup>b</sup> אי לאו … ותַקְּנִינְהוּ בתפלה וכ' were it not that Moses had said them (the words, ‘O God, great, mighty and terrible’), and the men of the Great Assembly had come and introduced them in the prayers, we could not dare to say them. Ib. תמני סרי תַּקּוּן וכ' eighteen benedictions they have ordained, nineteen they have not. Ib. 40
<sup>b</sup> ברכה דלא תַקִּינוּ רבנן a benediction which the Rabbis have not introduced. B. Bath. 90
<sup>b</sup> רב פפא … ת' כיילא וכ' Rab Papa … introduced a measure of three Ḳ’fizas. Ib. אנא … תַּקִּינִי I have introduced a new measure; a. v. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<binyan-name>Af.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אַתְקֵין</binyan-form>

<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to establish</italic>.</definition>
<notes>. Targ. Prov. III, 19. Targ. Is. XXX, 33; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to prepare, arrange, set in order</italic> &c. (v.

<number>—3)</number>
<definition>

<notes> R. Hash. 34
<sup>a</sup> איתקין ר' אבהו וכ' (read: אַתְ'; Ms. M. הִתְקִין Hebr.) R. A. introduced the custom in Cæsaræa of sounding one T’ḳiʿah, three notes of Sh’barim, and one T’ḳiʿah. Ib. מאי א' what has he improved (what has he achieved with his ordinance)? Gitt. 86
<sup>a</sup> א' רב יהודה וכ' Rab Judah introduced the formula for the sale of slaves: ‘this slave &c.’ Y. Ḥag. I, 76
<sup>c</sup> ר' יודה … למַתְקְנָא לון וכ' (or למְתַקְּנָא, 
<italic>Pa.</italic>) R. Judah the Nasi sent out R. Ḥ…, that they should pass the towns … to institute teachers of Bible and of Mishnah for them; Midr. Till. to Ps. CXXVII; Lam. R. introd., beg. דיפקון ויַתְקְנוּן קרייתא וכ' (or ויתַקְּנוּן) that they should go and improve (the education of) the towns in Palestine; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<head-word>תַּקָּנָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (תָּקַן) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>remedy</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥag. 5
<sup>a</sup>, v. מָצָא. Ib. 15
<sup>a</sup>
<pgbrk id="pg1693" />מה כלי … יש להם ת' … יש לו ת' as gold and glass vessels, even when they are broken, can be mended (remolten), so may a scholar, even if he has sinned, be restored (through repentance); Ab. d’R. N. ch. XXIV. Y. Sabb. IX, end, 12
<sup>b</sup>, v. עוֹלָמִית; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>arrangement, ordinance, improvement, measure for the public welfare, reform</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. 10
<sup>a</sup> הואיל ותַקָּנַת חכמים וכ' since it (the K’thubah) is merely a Rabbinical ordinance, she can collect her jointure only from the worst land. Ib. בתַקָּנָתָם, v. יָעַל. Gitt. IV, 6 we must not help captives to escape, מפני תקנת השבויין this regulation was made for the benefit of the (remaining) captives (who would be ill-treated after one escaped). Ib. V, 5 it has been decreed that if a joist is stolen and put into a building, the owner must accept the money for it, מפני תקנת השבים as a measure for the benefit of repentant sinners. R. Hash. I, 4 מפני תקנת קרבן in order to be able to regulate the sacrifices (for the New Year’s day). B. Kam. 115
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. תקנת השוק, v. שׁוּק III. Y. R. Hash. IV, 59
<sup>b</sup> bot. ויש ת' אחר הת' is there an ordinance after an ordinance, i.e. can a measure enacted by the Rabbis be extended by another enactment?; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. תַּקָּנוֹת</plural-form>. Bab. ib. 31
<sup>b</sup> זו אחת מתשע ת' וכ' (not אחד) this is one of the nine reforms introduced by R. J. ben Zaccai. B. Kam. 82
<sup>a</sup> עשר ת' וכ' (not עשרה) Ezra made ten regulations: that reading from the Law should take place on Mondays and Thursdays &c. Men. 51
<sup>b</sup> שתי ת' וכ' (not שני) two reforms were introduced by the Rabbis &c. B. Mets. 112
<sup>b</sup> הני הילכתא נינהו הני ת' נינהו do you call these 
<italic>hălakhoth</italic> (legal decisions)? these are reforms (changing the Biblical law). Ib. ת' קבועות measures deserving to be perpetuated (to supersede the Biblical law); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00904">

<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>remedy</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. Num. IV, 19.—Meg. 3
<sup>a</sup> מאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיה וכ' what is his remedy (what shall he do)? Let him read the Sh’mʿa. Snh. 7
<sup>a</sup> ולא הויא ת' לעולם and there would never be a remedy for them; אפשר … ת' בתשובה there might have been a remedy for them through repentance. Zeb. 76
<sup>a</sup> אית ליה ת' ברעייה there is a remedy for it by letting it go to pasture; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>measure, ordinance, reform</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Meg. 2
<sup>a</sup> אתו רבנן ועקרו ת' דתקינו וכ' will the Rabbis abolish an institution introduced by the men of the Great Assembly? Ib. אפי' בזמן הזה איתא להאי ת' this regulation is maintained even in our days (after the destruction of the Temple). B. Kam. 96
<sup>a</sup> ת' לעכו"ם וכ' shall we introduce a measure for the benefit of a gentile (robber, as we do for the benefit of a repentant Jew)? B. Mets. 5
<sup>a</sup> sq. שבועת … ת' היא ות' לת' לא עבדינן R. Naḥman’s oath of equity (v. הֶיסֵּת) is a reform, and we do not introduce a reform for a reform, i.e. the Rabbinical ordinance that, when one of the litigants is unfit to make oath, the opponent must swear, applies only to cases in which the oath is required by Biblical law, but not to cases in which the oath is itself a Rabbinical requirement; Shebu. 41
<sup>a</sup>; 46
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>17</sup> Caleb is named Tekoa (I Chr. II, 24), שת' לבו לאביו וכ' because he fastened his heart on his father in heaven. Yeb. 109
<sup>b</sup> תּוֹקֵעַ עצמו לדבר הלכה he who nails himself to the matter of the law, i.e. confines himself to study, and is remiss in practical conduct; ואיבעית אימא תוקע … בדיינא וכ' or I may explain, ‘he who nails himself to the matter of the law’ refers to a judge before whom a case comes, and he having learned a certain 
<italic>hălakhah</italic> decides by analogy, while there is a greater scholar than he whom he fails to consult; a. e.—

<sup>c</sup> והסכין ת' בלבו with the knife sticking in his heart; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>

<italic>to shout</italic>, esp. 
<italic>to blow</italic> (
<italic>a horn</italic>).</definition>

<sup>b</sup>. Ib. ת' באזנו וכ' if one blew on a horn into a person’s ear, and made him deaf; a. e.—Esp. 
<italic>a</italic>) 
<italic>to blow the Shofar at services; b</italic>) 
<italic>to sound the plain note</italic> (תְּקִיעָה). R. Hash. III, 5 בר"ה תּוֹקְעִין בשל זכרים on New Year’s day they blow on a ram’s horn. Ib. 8 אין מעכבין … מלִתְקוֹעַ we do not prevent children from blowing the Shofar (on the Sabbath). Ib. 9 תוקע ומריע ותוקע, v. רוּעַ I. Taan. <sup>a</sup>) התוקע לחבירו he who slaps his neighbor on the ear; oth. opin. who shouts into his neighbor’s ear.]</notes></sense></senses>

<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to seize, overpower</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yeb. 54
<sup>a</sup> ותְקָפַתּוֹ יבמתו (not ותקפתה) and his sister-in-law seized (forced) him. Ib. תְּקָפוּהוּ נכרים וכ' gentiles seized him, and coupled them. B. Mets. 6
<sup>a</sup> תְּקָפָהּ אחד בפנינו if one (of the two litigants) seized it (the object in dispute) in the presence of the court. Ib.
<sup>b</sup> תְּקָפוֹ כהן if a priest seized it (the lamb of doubtful first birth). Ab. Zar. 23
<sup>a</sup> יצרו תוֹקְפוֹ his passion overpowers him. Midr. Till. to Ps. XIX, 14 (ref. to איתם ib., with play on איתן) אלו תוֹקְפֵי עבירות this refers to those who conquer sin; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (with על) 
<italic>to rest heavily upon, be hard</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ab. III, 8 תָּקְפָה עליו משנתו if his study was too hard for him (and therefore he forgot again what he had learned); Men. 99
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00909">

<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to seize, hold firmly</italic>.</definition>

<italic>Ittof.</italic>).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be strong, become powerful</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Ex. I, 7 (Y. ed. Vien. אַתְקִיפוּ 
<italic>Af.</italic>). Ib. XIX, 19 (Y. ed. Wil. תַּקִּיף, read: תָּקֵיף). Targ. Gen. XLI, 57. Targ. O. Deut. XXXI, 6, sq. Targ. Jud. VII, 11 יִתְקְפָן ed. Lag. (ed. Wil. יתקוף, corr. acc.); a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be heavy, rest heavily upon, be hard</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. O. Gen. XLVII, 20 (Y. תַּקִּיף). Targ. I Sam. V, 7 (ed. Wil. תַּקִּרפַת).—Gitt. 77
<sup>b</sup> ת' ליה עלמא the world was heavy for him, i.e. he felt very ill (v. קַלִּיל II). Kidd. 22
<sup>b</sup> חזייה דתָקיף ליה עלמא טובא (or דתְקֵיף) he saw that he was very sick; a. fr.—Ned. 91
<sup>a</sup>, v. infra.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition> (with רוגזא, or sub. רוגזא) 
<italic>to be vehement, hot, excited</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Gen. XXX, 2. Targ. Ex. XXII, 23. Targ. Ps. XVIII, 8 ת' ליה; Targ. II Sam. XXII, 8 ת' רוגזיה. Targ. Jon. IV, 4; 9 תְּקוֹף ed. Lag. (ed. Wil. תְּקֵיף, a. תקוף). Targ. Gen. IV, 6 (Y. ed. Vien. תַּקִּיף); a. fr.—Yeb. 63
<sup>b</sup> מִתְקֵיף תְּקִיפָא she is irascible, v. עֲבַר 
<italic>Ithpe.</italic>—Ned. 91
<sup>a</sup> זמנין דתקיף לה מן גברא sometimes she has a strong feeling against her husband; [oth. interpret.: she has a strong passion for another man].—4) 
<italic>to get hot, ferment, get sour</italic>. B. Mets. 64
<sup>a</sup> אי תַקְפָה ברשותך if it should get sour, it shall be considered in thy possession (it shall be thy loss). Ib. 83
<sup>a</sup> זבני … ותְקִיפוּ להו I bought three hundred barrels of wine for thee, and they turned sour; ארבע … כי תְקִיפֵי וכ' (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 4) if four hundred barrels turn sour, this must have been rumored about; Yalk. Ex. 346 כי תַקְפֵי; Ber. 5
<sup>b</sup> (En Yaʿăḳob אִיתְּקוּף 
<italic>Ithpe)</italic>; a. e.</notes></sense></senses>

<number>1)</number>

<italic>the heart of</italic>).</definition>

<sense>
<number>—2)</number>

<sup>a</sup> תַּקְּפֵיה עייליה וכ' he seized him and brought him to the school-house.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>

<xref rid="V00887">תַּקִּיף</xref>)

<italic>to grow strong</italic>.</definition>

<sense>
<number>—3)</number>

<italic>to seize, take hold of, to cause to seize</italic>.</definition>

<number>—4)</number>

<italic>Af.</italic> incorr.); a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be hardened</italic>.</definition>
<notes>. Targ. Ex. VII, 13; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>

<italic>to get sour</italic>, v. supra.—[Targ.</definition>
<notes> Y. Num. XXXVI, 7 תיתקף, read: תיסתקף, v. סְקַף I.]</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<sup>a</sup> ת' של תורה וכ' the translation of the Torah was composed by Onkelos the proselyte from the mouth (by direction) of R. El. and R. <notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>shield</italic> (of twisted osiers &c.).</definition>
<notes> Sabb. VI, 4. Kel. XXIV, 1 שלשה תריסין הן ת' כפוף וכ' there are three sorts of shields (with regard to levitical cleanness): the bent shield (which may be used as an improvised seat) is unclean as 
<italic>midras</italic> (v. מִדְרָס), and that with which they play in the camp &c., v. דִּיצָה. Midr. Till. to Ps. I; Yalk. ib. 833 (ref. to מגן, Ps. LXXXIV, 1</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> [read:] הת' שמקיף וכ' (איסקוטא פרסאה, איש', being a gloss, v. 
<xref rid="I00016">טַארְגָא</xref>) that is the 
<italic>taris</italic>, which protects man on three sides, contrad. to צִנָּה.</definition>
<notes> Ab. IV, 11 תשובה … כת' בפני הפורענות repentance and good deeds are as a shield against misfortune; [oth. opin: as a 
<italic>shutter</italic>, v. infra).—Pl. תָּרִיסִין. Kel. l. c. Ber. 27
<sup>b</sup>; Bekh. 36
<sup>a</sup> בעלי ת' shield-bearers, i.e. great debaters.—2) (cmp. נַעַל) 
<italic>shutter.—</italic>
<plural-form>Pl. as ab. Bets. I, 5 אין מסלקין את הת' וכ'</plural-form> you must not remove (take apart) shutters on the Holy Day; expl. ib. 11
<sup>b</sup> תְּרֵיסֵי חנויות shutters of shops. Y. ib. I, 60
<sup>c</sup>, v. לָחַם I; Y. Sabb. XII, 13
<sup>c</sup> התירצין (read: התְּרִיצִין).</notes></sense></senses></entry>
